rationale: The 835 shows CO-29 on both service lines. The 837P (ISA date Oct 15, 2025) was sent CLM05-3=1 (new original), ~9 months after the Jan 19, 2025 DOS; payer denied as untimely. However, the 277CA (Jan 27, 2025) carries STC A2:20 — the original claim was accepted by the clearinghouse 8 days after DOS, well within any commercial timely filing window. The CO-29 is disputable; appeal with the 277CA acceptance as proof of timely original filing.

root_cause.explanation: Both lines CO-29. The Oct 15, 2025 resubmission (CLM05-3=1) arrived ~9 months post-DOS; payer treated it as a late new original. The 277CA (STC A2:20, Jan 27, 2025) proves original acceptance 8 days after the Jan 19, 2025 DOS.

next_action.detail: Appeal citing the 277CA (STC*A2:20*20250127) as proof of timely original filing — accepted 8 days after DOS. Dispute the payer's receipt date; do not plead forgiveness. N211 is Medicare-specific; ERISA commercial appeal rights apply. Appeal clock runs from the Nov 1, 2025 remit.

evidence.fact: CAS*CO*29 on both lines (97110:GP $91.91, 97140:GP $46.71); CLP07=2530598850660 confirms adjudication; MOA N211 at claim level.
CLM05-3=1 (new original frequency); ISA date 2025-10-15, ~9 months after DOS 2025-01-19 — payer treated this as a late new claim.
STC*A2:20*20250127: claim TRC75364521 accepted by clearinghouse January 27, 2025 — 8 days after DOS. This is proof of timely original filing.
EB*1 active coverage effective 2024-01-01, no termination date; member was covered on DOS 2025-01-19. Eligibility is not a factor.

citations.rule: Proof of an accepted submission inside the window → appeal with the clearinghouse acceptance report; dispute the receipt date, don't plead forgiveness.
CO-29 with no exception → do_not_resubmit; an exception exists here (277CA A2:20 acceptance predates any plausible commercial filing window), so appeal is the correct path.
